neighbours.label: the object of a conveying verb (bring/take/carry someone or something to a place or person)
fire: The school van will drive them to the museum every Friday.
Could you bring me a glass of water from the kitchen?
A shuttle takes guests from the airport to the hotel.
We brought them some soup when they were sick.
The ferry carries cars and passengers across the strait.
Her uncle took us to the zoo on Saturday morning.
Please deliver them the package before noon.
The volunteers will transport patients to the clinic.
quiet: The school van will wait for them outside the museum every Friday.
Could you tell me where the glasses are in the kitchen?
A shuttle welcomes guests with music at the airport.
We thanked them for the soup when they were sick.
The ferry sails slowly across the strait at dawn.
Her uncle told us about the zoo on Saturday morning.
Please remind them about the package before noon.
The volunteers will thank patients at the clinic.

notes: Card: 'take them on trips', 'took the waiter with him', 'moving people or goods', 'brought me in', 'Bring them any questions'. Negative pole and logit effect: suppresses arrive/visit/come/bring, so the unit marks who or what gets moved. Probe: 'bring us' 0.69, 'take them to' 0.23, 'thanked them' 0.02. Near misses put the same pronouns after non-conveying verbs.
